questions.question: Which of the following pairs of Union Territories were merged to form a single Indian Union Territory in 2020?

options.text: Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• On **January 26, 2020**, the Union Territories of **Dadra and Nagar Haveli** and **Daman and Diu** were officially merged into a single Union Territory named **Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu**.
 
• This merger was carried out for better administrative efficiency and to reduce the duplication of resources in the governance of the two Union Territories.
 
• The merger was enacted through the **Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu (Merger of Union Territories) Act, 2019**, which was passed by Parliament in December 2019 and received presidential assent soon after. *Hence, the statement is correct.*
 
• The new Union Territory consists of **four districts**, namely Dadra, Nagar Haveli, Daman, and Diu. The capital of the merged Union Territory is **Daman**.
 
• This decision was taken as both Union Territories were geographically close and had similar cultural and historical backgrounds. *Hence, this statement is correct.*
 
• The merger reduced the total number of Union Territories in India from nine to eight after its implementation. *Hence, the statement is correct.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Dadra and Nagar Haveli:**

 
 
• This region was under Portuguese rule until its liberation in **1954**. It officially became a Union Territory of India in **1961**.
 
• The territory is known for its lush greenery, tribal population, and natural resources.
 
 
 
• **Daman and Diu:**
 
 
• Daman and Diu were also under Portuguese rule until their liberation in **1961**. It became a Union Territory in **1987** after Goa was granted statehood.
 
• Known for its beaches, cultural heritage, and Portuguese-style architecture, it is a popular tourist destination.
 
 
 
• **Reasons for Merger:**
 
 
• Both territories were geographically connected and had similar administrative, cultural, and linguistic traits.
 
• The merger aimed to streamline governance and reduce administrative costs by having a unified administration.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Union Territories in India:**

 
 
• India currently has **8 Union Territories**. These are governed directly by the Central Government.
 
• Union Territories are usually smaller in area and population compared to states and lack legislative powers in most cases.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context:**
 
 
• The Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu merger is a significant step in India's administrative restructuring in the 21st century.
 
• Such mergers reflect the government's intent to improve governance efficiency and ensure better resource allocation.

questions.question: The government has made efforts to boost financial inclusion. Which 2014 scheme aimed to provide universal banking access in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jan Dhan Yojana**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY)**, launched in **August 2014**, is a flagship scheme of the Government of India to promote **financial inclusion** by ensuring access to financial services like banking, savings, deposits, remittance, credit, insurance, and pension.
 
• It primarily aims to provide **universal access** to banking facilities, especially for the economically weaker sections of society.
 
• **Zero Balance Accounts:** Under this scheme, individuals can open a bank account without maintaining any minimum balance.
 
• **RuPay Debit Card:** Account holders are provided with a **RuPay debit card** to facilitate cashless transactions and access to ATMs.
 
• **Insurance Benefits:** The scheme offers an **accidental insurance cover** of up to **₹2 lakh** and a **life insurance cover** of **₹30,000** for eligible beneficiaries.
 
• **Mobile Banking Access:** It enables individuals to use **mobile banking** for financial transactions, enhancing digital inclusion.
 
• **Direct Benefit Transfers (DBT):** The scheme facilitates **direct transfer of subsidies** to beneficiaries' bank accounts, reducing leakages in government programs.
 
• By March 2023, **PMJDY accounts crossed 500 million**, showcasing its success in bringing unbanked individuals into the formal financial system.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **JAM Trinity:**

 
 
• **JAM** stands for **Jan Dhan-Aadhaar-Mobile**. It refers to the integration of these three components to deliver subsidies and financial benefits directly to the beneficiaries, reducing corruption and inefficiencies.
 
• **Jan Dhan:** Bank accounts under PMJDY serve as the foundation for financial inclusion.
 
• **Aadhaar:** The unique identification system enables targeted delivery of services and prevents duplication.
 
• **Mobile:** Mobile connectivity facilitates easy and quick financial transactions.
 
 
 
• **PMAY (Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana):**
 
 
• Launched in **2015**, this scheme aims to provide **affordable housing** to all by 2022, ensuring **housing for the economically weaker sections (EWS)** and low-income groups (LIG).
 
• It offers **credit-linked subsidies** for home loans and focuses on urban and rural areas.
 
 
 
• **MUDRA Yojana:**
 
 
• Launched in **2015**, this scheme provides financial support to **micro and small enterprises** through loans under the **Shishu, Kishor, and Tarun** categories.
 
• It aims to promote entrepreneurship and employment in the non-corporate sector.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Jan Dhan Yojana Impact:** It has significantly increased **financial literacy** and empowered marginalized sections of society by providing access to financial services.
 
• **Global Recognition:** PMJDY has been recognized as one of the **world's largest financial inclusion initiatives** by international organizations like the **World Bank**.
 
• **Future Goals:** The scheme aims to enhance **digital banking**, encourage savings, and ensure the socio-economic upliftment of the underprivileged.

questions.question: The 13th edition of the joint military exercise 'Ekuverin' 2025 was conducted in which country?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

questions.question: Which initiative is associated with the construction of individual household toilets in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Swachh Bharat Abhiyan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Swachh Bharat Abhiyan (Clean India Mission)** is a flagship program launched by the Government of India in **October 2014** by **Prime Minister Narendra Modi**.
 
• The mission aims to eliminate open defecation and improve sanitation across the country by constructing **individual household toilets**, public toilets, and promoting behavioral change.
 
• It is divided into two sub-missions: **Swachh Bharat Gramin** (for rural areas) and **Swachh Bharat Urban** (for urban areas). The rural component focuses on building household toilets to achieve 100% sanitation coverage. *Hence, this initiative is directly associated with the construction of individual household toilets.*
 
• The mission also includes components such as **solid waste management**, awareness campaigns, and promoting cleanliness in public spaces.
 
• The Swachh Bharat Mission has resulted in the construction of over **100 million toilets** and has significantly reduced open defecation practices in rural and urban India. *Hence, the correct option is Swachh Bharat Abhiyan.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **AMRUT (Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation):**

 
 
• This scheme focuses on improving urban infrastructure, such as water supply, sewerage systems, and urban transport, but it does not directly deal with individual household toilets. It targets cities with a population above 1 lakh.
 
 
 
• **Jal Jeevan Mission:**
 
 
• This mission aims to provide **safe and adequate drinking water** to all households in rural India through functional tap connections by **2024**. It does not focus on sanitation or toilets.
 
 
 
• **Smart Cities Mission:**
 
 
• This initiative focuses on developing **100 smart cities** in India, emphasizing urban planning, technology, and sustainable development. Sanitation is a component but not the primary focus.
 
 
 
• **Swachh Bharat Abhiyan:**
 
 
• The mission has played a pivotal role in achieving the goal of an **open defecation-free India** by **2019**, coinciding with the **150th birth anniversary** of Mahatma Gandhi.
 
• It promotes community participation and awareness-building campaigns, encouraging behavioral change in sanitation practices.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Achievements of Swachh Bharat Abhiyan:**

 
 
• The mission has constructed over **100 million household toilets**, effectively reducing open defecation rates.
 
• It has contributed to improving **health and hygiene** by reducing waterborne diseases and improving sanitation standards.
 
 
 
• **Global Recognition:**
 
 
• The Swachh Bharat Mission has been recognized globally as a successful sanitation initiative and has inspired similar programs in other countries.

questions.question: The Mauryan empire was founded by Chandragupta Maurya in which of the following years?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**322 BCE**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Mauryan Empire** was founded by **Chandragupta Maurya** in **322 BCE**. It marked the beginning of one of the most significant dynasties in Indian history.
 
• This empire was established after overthrowing the **Nanda Dynasty**, which ruled over Magadha.
 
• Chandragupta Maurya, with the guidance of his mentor **Chanakya (Kautilya)**, laid the foundation of a centralized state that encompassed a large part of the Indian subcontinent. *Hence, option 4 is correct.*
 
• The Mauryan Empire was known for its strong centralized administration, efficient governance, and military strength, which helped Chandragupta consolidate his rule.
 
• The empire expanded its territory under Chandragupta Maurya and later under his successors like **Bindusara** and **Ashoka**. Chandragupta Maurya is credited with laying the groundwork for this large empire. *Hence, statement is correct.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Chandragupta Maurya:**

 
 
• **Chandragupta Maurya** was the first emperor of the Mauryan Empire and ruled from **322 BCE to 298 BCE**.
 
• He was mentored by **Chanakya**, also known as **Kautilya**, a renowned scholar and strategist. Chanakya’s political treatise, **Arthashastra**, laid the foundation for effective governance in the Mauryan Empire.
 
 
 
• **Key Features of the Mauryan Empire:**
 
 
• The Mauryan Empire was one of the largest empires in ancient India, covering parts of modern-day India, Pakistan, Afghanistan, and Bangladesh.
 
• The centralized administration under the Mauryan rulers ensured efficient governance and stability across the empire.
 
• **Example:** Chandragupta established a capital at **Pataliputra** (modern-day Patna), which became the administrative and political center of the empire.
 
 
 
• **Successors of Chandragupta Maurya:**
 
 
• **Bindusara:** Chandragupta’s son, who succeeded him, expanded the empire further into southern India.
 
• **Ashoka the Great:** Chandragupta’s grandson, who is known for his role in spreading Buddhism and the establishment of peace across the empire.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Chandragupta’s Rise to Power:**

 
 
• Chandragupta defeated the **Nanda Dynasty**, which was known for its oppressive rule, to establish the Mauryan Empire.
 
• He allied with **Alexander the Great’s successor**, Seleucus I Nicator, to strengthen his empire. The treaty allowed Chandragupta to acquire territories west of the Indus River.
 
 
 
• **Administrative Achievements:**
 
 
• The Mauryan Empire had a well-organized bureaucracy and infrastructure, including roads, trade routes, and irrigation systems.
 
• The **Arthashastra**, written by Chanakya, played a crucial role in shaping the empire’s administrative policies.
 
• The empire’s military strength and strategies helped in maintaining internal stability and defending against external invasions.

questions.question: In which of the following years did the Government of India disinvest 51% of shares of Bharat Aluminium Company Limited (BALCO) to Sterlite Industries (India) Limited, now Vedanta Limited?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2001**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bharat Aluminium Company Limited (BALCO)** was established as a public sector company in India to cater to the demand for aluminium production in the country.
 
• The **Government of India** decided to disinvest its stake in BALCO as part of its **economic liberalization policies** aimed at reducing government ownership in public enterprises and promoting privatization.
 
• In **2001**, the government disinvested **51% of its shares** in BALCO to **Sterlite Industries (India) Limited**, which is now known as **Vedanta Limited**. *Hence, the correct answer is 2001.*
 
• This move marked a significant step in the privatization of public sector enterprises in India, with Sterlite Industries acquiring majority ownership and operational control of BALCO.
 
• The disinvestment was considered controversial, as it faced opposition from employees and various political groups who expressed concerns about the impact of privatization on workers and national interests. *However, the disinvestment was eventually completed in 2001.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sterlite Industries (India) Limited:**

 
 
• **Sterlite Industries**, now known as **Vedanta Limited**, is a leading natural resources company in India that deals with mining, metals, and power generation.
 
• It acquired a majority stake in **BALCO** in **2001** as part of the government’s disinvestment program, enabling the company to expand its operations in the aluminium sector.
 
 
 
• **Privatization in India:**
 
 
• Privatization refers to the transfer of ownership and management of public sector enterprises to private entities.
 
• The **Government of India** adopted privatization policies in the 1990s as part of its broader economic reforms to improve efficiency, attract investment, and reduce fiscal burdens.
 
• **Example:** Alongside BALCO, other public sector enterprises like **Maruti Suzuki** and **Air India** have undergone privatization to varying extents.
 
 
 
• **Impact of BALCO Disinvestment:**
 
 
• The disinvestment allowed **Sterlite Industries** to modernize and expand BALCO's facilities, leading to increased aluminium production and improved operational efficiency.
 
• However, the process also faced criticism from workers’ unions and opposition parties due to concerns about job security and the valuation of the company.
 
• Despite the controversies, the privatization of BALCO is regarded as a landmark event in India’s disinvestment history.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Disinvestment Policy:**

 
 
• Disinvestment involves the government selling its stakes in public sector enterprises to private entities to reduce fiscal deficits and enhance operational efficiency.
 
• It is implemented by government bodies like the **Department of Investment and Public Asset Management (DIPAM).**
 
 
 
• **Significance of Aluminium Industry:**
 
 
• **Aluminium** is a versatile metal used in various industries, including construction, transportation, packaging, and electrical applications.
 
• India is one of the largest producers of aluminium in the world, with companies like **Hindalco Industries** and **BALCO** playing a key role in meeting domestic and international demand.

questions.question: At the 2025 British Book Awards gala in central London, who received the Freedom to Publish award?

• **Margaret Atwood** is renowned for her literary contributions, including novels such as **"The Handmaid's Tale"**, which critically examine themes of power, freedom, and societal control.
 
• The Freedom to Publish award aligns with Margaret Atwood's long-standing advocacy for creative and intellectual freedom. *Hence, this recognition is fitting.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• Her notable works include **"The Handmaid's Tale"**, **"Oryx and Crake"**, and **"Alias Grace"**. Many of her writings critically examine themes of oppression and freedom.
 
• Atwood has received numerous awards, including the **Booker Prize** and the **Governor General's Award**, solidifying her status as a literary icon.
 
 
 
• **The Freedom to Publish award:**
 
 
• This award is presented to individuals or organizations that demonstrate courage and commitment to upholding the right to publish freely without censorship.
 
• It highlights the importance of freedom of expression, which is essential for creativity, democracy, and intellectual discourse.
 
• Margaret Atwood's recognition with this award is a testament to her contributions to literature and advocacy for creative freedom.
 
 
 
• **Other notable authors:**
 
 
• **JK Rowling:** Known for her **Harry Potter series**, Rowling has faced controversies related to freedom of speech but is not associated with the 2025 award.
 
• **Salman Rushdie:** An author famous for **"The Satanic Verses"**, Rushdie is a vocal advocate for freedom of expression but was not the recipient of this award in 2025.
 
• **Hilary Mantel:** Known for her **Wolf Hall trilogy**, Mantel has been recognized for her literary achievements but did not receive the Freedom to Publish award.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Significance of the Freedom to Publish award:**

 
 
• The award underscores the importance of resisting censorship and promoting intellectual freedom in literature and publishing.
 
• It serves as a reminder of the challenges faced by authors and publishers in ensuring free access to creative works.
 
 
 
• **Margaret Atwood's advocacy:**
 
 
• Atwood has consistently championed the right to creative freedom, evident in her works and public appearances.
 
• Her contributions to literature and her steadfast support for intellectual and creative liberties make her a deserving recipient of the award.

questions.question: Which hazardous pesticide was agreed to be eliminated under the Stockholm Convention held in Geneva in 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chlorpyrifos**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chlorpyrifos** is a widely used organophosphate pesticide, primarily for agricultural purposes to control pests like insects and termites.
 
• The **Stockholm Convention**, an international treaty aimed at eliminating or reducing the use of hazardous chemicals, agreed to eliminate Chlorpyrifos due to its adverse environmental and health impacts.
 
• Chlorpyrifos has been linked to significant health concerns, including **neurotoxicity**, developmental disorders, and environmental contamination. *Hence, it was targeted for elimination.*
 
• The **2025 Geneva meeting** under the Stockholm Convention specifically focused on eliminating hazardous pesticides like Chlorpyrifos to ensure sustainable agricultural practices and protect global biodiversity.
 
• Chlorpyrifos persists in the environment and can contaminate soil, water, and air, harming non-target organisms such as pollinators and aquatic species. *Hence, its elimination was deemed essential for ecological conservation.*
 
• The decision aligns with the **United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)**, particularly Goal 3 (Good Health and Well-Being) and Goal 15 (Life on Land), which emphasize reducing pollution and promoting sustainable ecosystems.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Chlorpyrifos:**

 
 
• **Chlorpyrifos** is an organophosphate pesticide first introduced in **1965**. It is used to control pests on crops, animals, and buildings.
 
• It is highly toxic to humans and animals, causing **neurological damage**, respiratory issues, and developmental delays in children.
 
• Countries like **India, the United States, and Australia** have been significant users of Chlorpyrifos. However, many nations have started banning or restricting its use due to health and environmental concerns.
 
 
 
• **Stockholm Convention:**
 
 
• The **Stockholm Convention**, established in **2001**, aims to eliminate or reduce the production and use of Persistent Organic Pollutants (POPs).
 
• POPs like Chlorpyrifos are chemicals that persist in the environment, accumulate in living organisms, and pose risks to human health and ecosystems.
 
• The convention involves over **180 countries**, including major global stakeholders, to ensure collaborative efforts in combating hazardous chemicals.
 
 
 
• **Other Options:**
 
 
• **Glyphosate:** A widely used herbicide, often debated for its environmental and health impacts but not yet agreed upon for elimination under the Stockholm Convention.
 
• **DDT:** A pesticide banned in several countries due to its ecological and health impacts, though used selectively for malaria control in some regions.
 
• **Atrazine:** A herbicide commonly used for weed control but under scrutiny for groundwater contamination and hormonal disruption.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Health Impact of Chlorpyrifos:**

 
 
• It is a **neurotoxin** affecting the central nervous system, particularly in children, leading to developmental and behavioral disorders.
 
• Exposure can occur through contaminated food, water, or air, posing risks to agricultural workers and nearby communities.

• **The hot weather season in India** typically falls between **March and May**, marking the pre-monsoon period in the country. This is the time when temperatures rise significantly, particularly in northern and central India.
 
• During this period, the **northern plains** of India experience extremely high temperatures, sometimes exceeding **45 degrees Celsius**, while the southern regions are relatively moderate but still warm.
 
• The hot weather season is characterized by the presence of dry and hot winds known as **“Loo”**, especially in the northern plains. These winds aggravate the heat and make conditions harsh.
 
• This season also sees the development of **localized thunderstorms** known as “Nor’westers” or “Kalbaisakhi,” particularly in regions like **West Bengal**, Odisha, and Assam.
 
• In **peninsular India**, the temperatures are comparatively lower due to the moderating influence of the **oceans**, but it is still considered the hot weather season.

__
 
• **Characteristics of Indian Seasons:**

 
 
• **Winter Season** (December to February): This is the coldest season in India, with temperatures dropping significantly, especially in the northern regions.
 
• **Summer/Hot Weather Season** (March to May): Marked by high temperatures, dry winds, and occasional thunderstorms.
 
• **Monsoon Season** (June to September): Characterized by heavy rainfall due to the southwest monsoon winds.
 
• **Post-Monsoon/Autumn Season** (October to November): This transitional period sees a reduction in rainfall and an onset of cooler weather.
 
 
 
• **Temperature Variations:**
 
 
• The northern plains experience temperatures above **45°C**, while coastal and southern regions are cooler due to proximity to the sea.
 
• Regions like **Rajasthan, Gujarat, and Madhya Pradesh** face extreme heat during the hot weather season.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Hot Weather Season:**
 
 
• This season is crucial for the formation of **monsoon winds**, as the intense heating over the Indian subcontinent creates a low-pressure zone, attracting moist winds from the Indian Ocean.

• **Impact of “Loo” Winds:**

 
 
• The hot winds known as “**Loo**” are a notable feature of this season. They are dry and extremely hot, causing dehydration and heatstrokes.
 
• These winds are prevalent in states like **Punjab, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, and Rajasthan**.
 
 
 
• **Weather Patterns:**
 
 
• **Nor’westers** are sudden, violent thunderstorms that bring temporary relief from the heat in eastern India, especially in **West Bengal, Assam, and Odisha**.
 
• These thunderstorms are also accompanied by strong winds and heavy rainfall, benefiting crops like **jute and rice**.

questions.question: What is the relation between the speed of sound (v), its wavelength (λ) and time period (T)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**v = λ / T**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Relation between speed, wavelength, and time period:** The speed of sound (**v**) in a medium is related to its wavelength (**λ**) and time period (**T**) by the formula: **v = λ / T**. This is a fundamental equation in wave mechanics.
 
• **Wavelength (λ):** This is the distance between two consecutive crests or troughs of a wave. It is measured in **meters (m)**.
 
• **Time Period (T):** This is the time taken for one complete oscillation or wave cycle. It is measured in **seconds (s)**.
 
• **Speed of sound (v):** This is the rate at which sound waves propagate through a medium. It is measured in **meters per second (m/s)**.
 
• The relationship can also be expressed in terms of **frequency** (f), as f = 1/T. Substituting f in the above formula gives v = λ × f.
 
• The formula highlights that the speed of sound is directly proportional to the wavelength and inversely proportional to the time period.
 
• *Hence, the correct answer is v = λ / T.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Wave Properties:**

 
 
• **Wavelength (λ):** It determines the spatial length of a wave and is inversely proportional to frequency for a constant speed of sound.
 
• **Time Period (T):** It is inversely related to frequency. A shorter time period corresponds to a higher frequency wave.
 
• **Frequency (f):** It is the number of oscillations per second, measured in **Hertz (Hz)**. Frequency is related to time period as f = 1/T.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Wave Mechanics:**
 
 
• **Acoustics:** Understanding the speed of sound is crucial in designing auditoriums and music halls.
 
• **Sonar Technology:** The relation between speed, wavelength, and time period is used in sonar systems for underwater exploration.
 
• **Communication:** Wave mechanics principles are applied in designing communication systems like radio and television.
 
 
 
• **Factors Affecting Speed of Sound:**
 
 
• The speed of sound depends on the **medium** through which it travels. It is faster in solids, slower in liquids, and slowest in gases.
 
• Temperature, pressure, and density of the medium also influence the speed of sound. For example, sound travels faster in warm air compared to cold air.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Alternative Representation:**

 
 
• The speed of sound can also be written as **v = λ × f**, where **f** is the frequency of the wave.
 
• This equation highlights the inverse relationship between wavelength and frequency when the speed is constant.
 
 
 
• **Practical Examples:**
 
 
• **Example:** In musical instruments, the pitch of a note is determined by the frequency of the sound wave, which is indirectly related to its time period.
 
• **Example:** In radar systems, the speed of electromagnetic waves is used to calculate distances using similar principles.

questions.question: Which classical Sanskrit play was written by Kalidasa?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Abhijnana-Shakuntalam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kalidasa**, one of the greatest classical Sanskrit playwrights and poets, wrote **Abhijnana-Shakuntalam**, considered a masterpiece of Sanskrit literature.
 
• **Abhijnana-Shakuntalam**, often translated as "The Recognition of Shakuntala," is a play that revolves around the love story of King Dushyanta and Shakuntala, a maiden of extraordinary beauty.
 
• The play is famous for its rich poetic descriptions, emotional depth, and intricate portrayal of human relationships.
 
• **Kalidasa** is also credited with other celebrated works such as **Raghuvamsha** and **Kumarasambhava**, but **Abhijnana-Shakuntalam** stands out as his most renowned play.
 
• The story of **Abhijnana-Shakuntalam** is based on an episode from the **Mahabharata**, specifically the tale of Shakuntala and King Dushyanta from the **Adi Parva**.
 
• The work has been widely translated into numerous languages and has had a profound influence on Indian and global literature. It was the first Sanskrit work to be translated into European languages in the 18th century, making Kalidasa internationally recognized.
 
• **Abhijnana-Shakuntalam** embodies the classical Sanskrit theatrical tradition, adhering to the rules of dramaturgy outlined in the **Natyashastra**.
 
• The correct answer is **Abhijnana-Shakuntalam**, as it is authored by Kalidasa and widely revered as one of the greatest contributions to Indian classical literature.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Kalidasa’s Contribution to Literature:**

 
 
• **Kalidasa** is renowned for his sophisticated and elegant style of writing, blending nature, emotions, and divine imagery seamlessly.
 
• He is often regarded as the **Shakespeare of India** due to his unparalleled contributions to drama and poetry in ancient Sanskrit literature.
 
• His works, apart from **Abhijnana-Shakuntalam**, include **Meghaduta** (The Cloud Messenger), **Kumarasambhava** (The Birth of Kumara), and **Raghuvamsha** (The Lineage of Raghu).
 
 
 
• **About the Play Abhijnana-Shakuntalam:**
 
 
• The play is divided into **seven acts**, depicting the journey of love, separation, and eventual reunion between King Dushyanta and Shakuntala.
 
• The central theme revolves around the concept of **love, memory, and recognition**, with a strong emphasis on destiny and divine intervention.
 
• The title, "Abhijnana," refers to the ring of recognition that plays a pivotal role in reuniting the lovers after a period of separation caused by a curse.
 
 
 
• **Other Options Explained:**
 
 
• **Mudrarakshasa:** Written by **Vishakhadatta**, this historical play focuses on the political strategies of Chanakya and the establishment of Chandragupta Maurya’s rule. *Not authored by Kalidasa.*
 
• **Svapnavasavadattam:** Written by **Bhasa**, this play narrates the story of King Udayana and his queen Vasavadatta. *Not authored by Kalidasa.*
 
• **Mrichchhakatika:** Also known as "The Little Clay Cart," this play was authored by **Shudraka** and deals with themes of love, morality, and social issues. *Not authored by Kalidasa.*
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Influence of Abhijnana-Shakuntalam:**

 
 
• **International Acclaim:** It was one of the first Sanskrit plays to be translated into European languages, introducing Indian literature to the Western world.
 
• **Translation:** The German translation by **Sir William Jones** in 1789 greatly popularized the play in Europe.
 
• **Cultural Significance:** The story of Shakuntala is deeply embedded in Indian culture, inspiring numerous art forms, including paintings, music, and dance.

questions.question: Diabetes mellitus is caused by the inadequate secretion of which hormone?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Insulin**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Insulin** is a hormone secreted by the **pancreas**, specifically by the beta cells of the Islets of Langerhans. It plays a critical role in regulating blood sugar levels in the body.
 
• The primary function of insulin is to help glucose, obtained from food, enter the cells of the body where it is used for energy. If the secretion of insulin is inadequate, glucose cannot be absorbed by the cells effectively, leading to a condition known as **hyperglycemia** (high blood sugar levels).
 
• This inadequate secretion or function of insulin is the primary cause of **Diabetes Mellitus**, a chronic metabolic disorder. *Hence, insulin is the correct answer.*
 
• In individuals with diabetes, either the pancreas does not produce enough insulin (Type 1 Diabetes) or the body’s cells do not respond effectively to insulin (Type 2 Diabetes).
 
• Proper management of diabetes involves the administration of insulin (for Type 1 Diabetes), medications, lifestyle changes, and dietary adjustments to maintain normal blood sugar levels.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Functions of Insulin:**

 
 
• Insulin facilitates the **uptake of glucose** by cells, especially muscle and fat cells, for energy production.
 
• It helps in the storage of excess glucose in the liver in the form of **glycogen** for future energy requirements.
 
• Insulin also plays a role in **fat metabolism** by promoting the storage of fats in adipose tissues and suppressing the breakdown of fat stores.
 
 
 
• **Symptoms of Diabetes Mellitus:**
 
 
• **Frequent urination** (polyuria), excessive thirst (polydipsia), and extreme hunger (polyphagia).
 
• **Fatigue, blurred vision**, slow wound healing, and unexplained weight loss are other common symptoms.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Hormones Listed in Options:**
 
 
• **Estrogen:** A female sex hormone responsible for regulating the reproductive system and secondary sexual characteristics in females. It is not involved in blood sugar regulation.
 
• **Adrenaline:** A hormone produced by the adrenal glands during stress, which increases heart rate and blood flow, but does not regulate glucose levels.
 
• **Thyroxine:** A hormone produced by the thyroid gland that regulates metabolism, but it does not have a direct role in blood sugar control.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Management of Diabetes:**

 
 
• Type 1 Diabetes is managed by administering **insulin injections** since the pancreas produces little to no insulin.
 
• Type 2 Diabetes is managed through a combination of **oral medications, dietary changes, physical activity**, and sometimes insulin if required.
 
 
 
• **Prevention of Diabetes:**
 
 
• Adopting a healthy lifestyle, including a **balanced diet, regular exercise**, and maintaining a healthy weight, can reduce the risk of developing Type 2 Diabetes.
 
• Regular health checkups and monitoring of **blood glucose levels** are crucial for early detection and management of diabetes.

__
 
• **Article 32** of the **Indian Constitution** provides the **Right to Constitutional Remedies**. This article empowers citizens to directly approach the Supreme Court for the enforcement of their fundamental rights.
 
• It is referred to as the **'heart and soul of the Constitution'**, as described by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, because it ensures that the fundamental rights are not just theoretical but are enforceable in a court of law.
 
• The Supreme Court is empowered to issue **writs** under Article 32 to enforce fundamental rights. These writs include **Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Certiorari, and Quo Warranto.**
 
• The right to move the Supreme Court under Article 32 is itself a **fundamental right**. This ensures that citizens have direct access to the apex court for the protection of their rights.
 
• This provision ensures that the judiciary acts as a guardian of fundamental rights and provides a mechanism for their enforcement. *Hence, Article 32 is correct.*
 
• **Article 31**, as per the original Constitution, dealt with the Right to Property. However, this right was removed as a fundamental right through the **44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978**, and is now a legal right under Article 300A. *Hence, this is incorrect.*
 
• **Article 30** provides the right of minorities to establish and administer educational institutions of their choice. *Hence, this is not the correct answer.*
 
• **Article 33** deals with the power of Parliament to modify the application of fundamental rights to the armed forces or forces charged with maintaining public order. *Hence, this is not the correct answer.*
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Article 32.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Writs under Article 32:**

 
 
• **Habeas Corpus:** A writ that is issued to produce a person who has been detained unlawfully before the court and justify the detention.
 
• **Mandamus:** A writ issued to a public official or body to perform a duty they are legally obligated to perform but have failed to do so.
 
• **Prohibition:** A writ issued to lower courts or tribunals to stop them from exceeding their jurisdiction.
 
• **Certiorari:** A writ issued to transfer a case from a lower court to a higher court or to quash the order of a lower court due to a lack of jurisdiction or error of law.
 
• **Quo Warranto:** A writ issued to challenge the authority of a person holding a public office.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Article 32:**
 
 
• It acts as a safeguard for citizens, ensuring the protection of their fundamental rights.
 
• It empowers the judiciary to check the legislative and executive branches, maintaining the balance of power.
 
• It underlines the concept of judicial review in India, which is a cornerstone of the Indian democracy.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Article 226:**
 
 
• **Article 226** of the Constitution empowers the High Courts to issue writs for the enforcement of not only fundamental rights but also for any other purpose.
 
• While Article 32 is restricted to fundamental rights, Article 226 has a wider scope, as it can deal with cases of legal rights as well.
 
• However, Article 32 is a fundamental right itself, whereas Article 226 is a constitutional right.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Judicial Interpretation:**

 
 
• The Supreme Court has emphasized that the right to approach the court under Article 32 cannot be suspended except during an emergency as per Article 359.
 
• The court has also ruled that even if alternative remedies are available, a person can directly approach the Supreme Court under Article 32 for enforcement of fundamental rights.
 
 
 
• **Role of Dr. B.R. Ambedkar:**
 
 
• Dr. Ambedkar referred to Article 32 as the most important article in the Indian Constitution, asserting that it was the very heart and soul of the document.

questions.question: Raja Ram Mohan Roy was an active social reformer who spoke greatly for the problems faced by women. He was an inseparable agent who brought down the social evil of ‘sati’. The reform association founded by him was:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Brahmo Samaj**__.

__
 
• **Raja Ram Mohan Roy** was a prominent social reformer who worked against various social evils, including the practice of **Sati**. He was instrumental in influencing the abolition of Sati through his persistent efforts and petitions to the British government. *Hence, the statement about him speaking greatly for women’s problems and being an agent in abolishing Sati is correct.*
 
• He founded the **Brahmo Samaj** in **1828**, which became a platform for advocating for social reforms such as equality, abolition of caste discrimination, and improvement of women's conditions in India. *Hence, the statement about the reform association founded by him is correct.*
 
• The **Brahmo Samaj** was established with the aim of purifying Hinduism and promoting monotheism, rejecting idolatry, and encouraging rationalism and scientific temper.
 
• The other options, such as **Arya Samaj** (founded by **Swami Dayanand Saraswati** in 1875), **Prarthana Samaj** (founded by **Atmaram Pandurang** in 1867), and **Ramakrishna Mission** (founded by **Swami Vivekananda** in 1897), were all founded by different leaders and served distinct purposes. These were not related to Raja Ram Mohan Roy’s initiatives. *Hence, these options are incorrect.*
 
• *Hence, the correct answer is Brahmo Samaj.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Brahmo Samaj:**

 
 
• The **Brahmo Samaj**, founded in **1828**, aimed to reform Indian society and eliminate harmful practices such as **Sati**, child marriage, and caste discrimination.
 
• It promoted **monotheism**, rejected idol worship, and encouraged rational thinking and social progress.
 
• The Brahmo Samaj played a significant role in spreading awareness about education and women's rights during the colonial period.
 
 
 
• **Other Reform Movements:**
 
 
• **Arya Samaj:** Founded by **Swami Dayanand Saraswati** in **1875**, it focused on Vedic teachings, abolition of caste, and promotion of education.
 
• **Prarthana Samaj:** Established by **Atmaram Pandurang** in **1867**, it aimed at social reform through religious practices, focusing on equality and women's rights.
 
• **Ramakrishna Mission:** Founded by **Swami Vivekananda** in **1897**, it promoted spiritual development, education, and welfare activities.
 
 
 
• **Raja Ram Mohan Roy’s Legacy:**
 
 
• Known as the **Father of Indian Renaissance**, Raja Ram Mohan Roy’s contributions include the abolition of Sati (achieved through the **Regulation XVII** in **1829**) and efforts toward women’s education.
 
• His advocacy for social reforms laid the foundation for modern Indian society, including reforms in religion, women’s rights, and education.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Legal Developments:**

 
 
• The abolition of Sati was achieved through **Regulation XVII** passed by Lord William Bentinck in **1829**, influenced by Raja Ram Mohan Roy’s advocacy.
 
• Raja Ram Mohan Roy’s efforts were pivotal in initiating reforms in colonial India, and his legacy continues to inspire movements for equality and social justice.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs of Indian states share international borders with Bangladesh?

__
 
• **India-Bangladesh Border:** India shares a long international border with Bangladesh, which spans over **4,096 km**. This is India's longest international border.
 
• **States Sharing Borders:** The Indian states that share borders with Bangladesh are **West Bengal, Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram**.
 
• **West Bengal:** West Bengal has the **longest border** with Bangladesh, stretching over **2,217 km**. It is significant due to its geographical location and cultural ties.
 
• **Tripura:** Tripura shares a border of approximately **856 km** with Bangladesh. It is a vital state for trade and cultural exchanges between the two nations.
 
• The pair mentioned in the correct option, **West Bengal and Tripura**, accurately represent states that share boundaries with Bangladesh. *Hence, the correct answer is West Bengal and Tripura.*

• **Sikkim:** Shares borders with Bhutan, Nepal, and China, but not Bangladesh.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Bangladesh is located to the east of India and shares boundaries with five Indian states: **West Bengal, Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram**.
 
• The border is characterized by **riverine terrain, plains, and hills**, making it geographically diverse.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context:**
 
 
• India and Bangladesh share strong historical ties dating back to the partition of India in **1947**, when East Bengal (now Bangladesh) became part of Pakistan.
 
• In **1971**, Bangladesh gained independence from Pakistan, and its borders with India became prominent in terms of trade, migration, and cultural exchanges.

• The borders between India and Bangladesh are crucial for **trade and connectivity**. Several border checkpoints facilitate economic exchanges.

• **Illegal migration**, smuggling, and border security are key challenges along the India-Bangladesh border.
 
• Efforts like the **Land Boundary Agreement** have helped address several issues, but vigilance remains critical.

questions.question: Public Interest Litigation (PIL) in India is primarily associated with which of the following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Judicial activism**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Public Interest Litigation (**PIL**) refers to the legal mechanism through which individuals or groups can approach the judiciary to address **issues of public interest** rather than private disputes.
 
• It is an important aspect of **Judicial Activism** in India, allowing courts to take up cases that aim to protect the rights of underprivileged sections of society or address significant public concerns.
 
• PILs in India can be filed by any citizen or organization, even if they are not directly impacted, to advocate for the **welfare of the general public**. This broad scope promotes inclusivity and justice.
 
• **Judicial activism** plays a crucial role in PIL as it enables the judiciary to interpret laws dynamically and take proactive measures to address societal and constitutional issues effectively.
 
• The concept of PIL was introduced in India by Justice **P.N. Bhagwati** and Justice **V.R. Krishna Iyer** in the late 1970s and early 1980s, aiming to make justice accessible to marginalized groups.
 
• Examples of PIL include cases addressing **environmental issues, human rights, corruption**, and ensuring accountability of government authorities.
 
• Judicial activism through PILs has led to landmark judgments in India, such as the Vishaka Guidelines for preventing sexual harassment and the enforcement of environmental protection measures.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Judicial activism.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Public Interest Litigation (PIL):**

 
 
• PIL is a mechanism in Indian judicial system that enables people to seek justice for issues affecting the larger public rather than individual disputes.
 
• It is a tool for enhancing **social justice** by addressing grievances of marginalized sections and resolving matters of **public importance**.
 
 
 
• **Judicial Activism:**
 
 
• **Judicial activism** refers to a proactive approach by the judiciary, where courts interpret laws dynamically to address societal changes and pressing issues.
 
• It is instrumental in protecting **fundamental rights**, ensuring government accountability, and promoting justice.
 
• **Example:** The Supreme Court has used judicial activism in cases like environmental protection, regulating corruption, and promoting gender equality.
 
 
 
• **Key Characteristics of PIL:**
 
 
• PILs can be filed in the Supreme Court under **Article 32** or in the High Courts under **Article 226** of the Constitution.
 
• They address a wide range of issues such as **human rights violations, environmental degradation, government accountability, and socio-economic issues.**
 
• PILs have played a significant role in ensuring justice for disadvantaged groups and addressing systemic issues.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Legal Provisions:**

 
 
• **Article 32:** Allows individuals to directly approach the Supreme Court for enforcement of fundamental rights, including filing PILs.
 
• **Article 226:** Enables High Courts to address issues of public interest and protect constitutional rights through PILs.
 
 
 
• **Landmark PIL Cases:**
 
 
• **Vishaka Guidelines:** Established legal provisions for preventing sexual harassment at workplaces.
 
• **MC Mehta Case:** Led to significant environmental conservation measures, including the regulation of industries causing pollution.
 
• **Olga Tellis Case:** Asserted the right to livelihood as part of fundamental rights.

questions.question: Centralised planning influenced India's industrial strategy for decades. Under which five-year plan were small-scale industries given specific protection and incentives?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Second Plan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Second Five-Year Plan (1956-1961)** in India was designed with a focus on rapid industrialization and the development of the public sector. This plan was inspired by the **Mahalanobis Model**, which emphasized the importance of heavy industries.
 
• During this plan, **small-scale industries** were given special attention, as these industries played a crucial role in providing employment, promoting regional balance, and ensuring equitable distribution of income.
 
• Specific **protection and incentives** were introduced for small-scale industries to encourage their growth. These included tax exemptions, subsidies, and easier access to credit.
 
• The plan also focused on **import substitution**, which meant promoting indigenous production to reduce reliance on imports, and small-scale industries were pivotal in achieving this objective.
 
• The emphasis on small-scale industries under the **Second Plan** was part of the broader strategy to develop a self-reliant economy and provide opportunities to rural and semi-urban populations. *Hence, this plan specifically targeted small-scale industries.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Second Five-Year Plan (1956-1961):**

 
 
• This plan was based on the **Mahalanobis Model**, which emphasized the development of heavy industries like steel, machinery, and chemicals for long-term economic growth.
 
• The **industrial sector** was given priority, and significant investments were made to develop the infrastructure necessary for industrial growth.
 
• The focus on small-scale industries was to ensure balanced regional development and to address unemployment issues, particularly in rural and semi-urban areas.
 
 
 
• **Small-Scale Industries (SSIs):**
 
 
• **Definition:** SSIs are industries with limited investment in machinery and equipment, as defined by government guidelines.
 
• **Features:** They employ local labor, use local raw materials, and cater to the domestic market, thus contributing to regional development and reducing urban migration.
 
• **Importance:** SSIs play a crucial role in generating employment, promoting entrepreneurship, and contributing to the GDP of the country.
 
 
 
• **Other Plans and Small-Scale Industries:**
 
 
• **First Plan (1951-1956):** Focused on agriculture and irrigation, with limited attention to industries.
 
• **Third Plan (1961-1966):** Focused on self-reliance and agriculture, with less emphasis on small-scale industries compared to the Second Plan.
 
• **Fourth Plan (1969-1974):** Focused on social justice and reduction of poverty, with some incentives for SSIs.
 
• **Fifth Plan (1974-1979):** Focused on poverty alleviation, rural development, and employment generation.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Incentives for Small-Scale Industries:**

 
 
• The government offered **tax exemptions** and subsidies to promote the growth of SSIs during the **Second Plan**.
 
• **Financial institutions like SIDBI** (Small Industries Development Bank of India) were established later to support SSIs with loans and credit facilities.
 
 
 
• **Role of SSIs in Economic Development:**
 
 
• SSIs contribute significantly to **employment generation**, especially in rural areas, thus reducing the pressure on urban centers.
 
• They promote **regional balance** by developing industries in less developed regions.

questions.question: What is the name of the glycoprotein produced in the liver that plays a crucial role in blood clotting?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fibrinogen**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Fibrinogen** is a glycoprotein produced by the **liver**. It plays a crucial role in the **blood clotting process**, which is essential for stopping bleeding during an injury.
 
• It is converted into **fibrin** by the action of an enzyme called **thrombin**. Fibrin forms a mesh or clot at the site of injury to prevent further blood loss.
 
• The presence of fibrinogen is vital for maintaining hemostasis, which is the process that stops bleeding and keeps the blood within damaged blood vessels.
 
• Fibrinogen is synthesized in the liver and circulates in the blood plasma. It is one of the **13 coagulation factors** involved in blood clotting.
 
• The concentration of fibrinogen in human blood plasma ranges from approximately **200 to 400 mg/dL**. Abnormal levels can indicate various medical conditions, such as inflammation, liver disease, or clotting disorders.
 
• *Hence, the correct answer is Fibrinogen.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Functions of Fibrinogen:**

 
 
• Fibrinogen is responsible for forming **fibrin clots** during the final stages of the coagulation cascade.
 
• It contributes to **wound healing** by stabilizing the clot and promoting tissue repair.
 
• Fibrinogen also plays a role in **immune responses** and inflammation by interacting with other proteins and cells.
 
 
 
• **Medical Importance:**
 
 
• **High levels of fibrinogen:** Elevated fibrinogen levels are associated with conditions like **cardiovascular diseases**, diabetes, or chronic inflammatory diseases.
 
• **Low levels of fibrinogen:** Deficiency of fibrinogen, known as **afibrinogenemia** or hypofibrinogenemia, can lead to excessive bleeding and difficulty in clot formation.
 
• **Diagnostic role:** Fibrinogen levels are measured in blood tests to evaluate clotting ability and diagnose bleeding disorders.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with other options:**
 
 
• **Cadherin:** Cadherins are cell adhesion molecules involved in maintaining tissue structure, not in blood clotting.
 
• **Mucins:** Mucins are glycoproteins found in mucus, playing a role in lubrication and protection, not clotting.
 
• **Selectin:** Selectins are adhesion molecules involved in immune cell trafficking, unrelated to clot formation.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **History of Fibrinogen:**

 
 
• Fibrinogen was first identified in **1856** by Alexander Schmidt, a scientist known for his work on blood coagulation.
 
• Its role in clot formation was further elucidated in the early 20th century, contributing to advancements in hematology.
 
 
 
• **Clinical Applications:**
 
 
• Fibrinogen is used as a therapeutic agent in managing bleeding disorders, such as during surgery or in patients with congenital fibrinogen deficiency.
 
• It is also a marker for assessing the risk of **thrombosis** and cardiovascular diseases.

questions.question: The foundation day anniversaries of which two Indian states was celebrated on 20 February 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Arunachal Pradesh and Mizoram**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Arunachal Pradesh** and **Mizoram** were both established as states on **20 February 1987**. Their foundation day anniversaries are celebrated annually on this date.
 
• **Arunachal Pradesh** was initially a Union Territory before becoming a full-fledged state in **1987**. The state is known for its rich cultural heritage, diverse tribal communities, and stunning natural landscapes.
 
• **Mizoram**, which was also a Union Territory, achieved statehood on the same day in **1987**. Mizoram is characterized by its lush green hills, vibrant festivals, and unique Mizo culture.
 
• The formation of these states was a significant milestone in India's administrative and political history, reflecting the government’s efforts to address regional aspirations and cultural diversity.
 
• Both states were established under the **State Reorganization process**, which is guided by **Article 3 of the Indian Constitution**. This article empowers the Parliament to create new states and alter the boundaries or names of existing states.
 
• Celebrating their foundation day highlights the importance of regional identity, cultural pride, and the progress achieved since their formation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Arunachal Pradesh:**

 
 
• Located in the northeastern region of India, it shares international borders with **China, Bhutan, and Myanmar**.
 
• Known as the "Land of the Dawn-Lit Mountains," Arunachal Pradesh is famous for its scenic beauty, including **Tawang Monastery**, which is one of the largest monasteries in Asia.
 
• The state is home to numerous indigenous tribes, such as the **Adi, Nyishi, Apatani, and Monpa**, who contribute to its rich cultural diversity.
 
 
 
• **Mizoram:**
 
 
• Located in the northeastern part of India, Mizoram shares borders with **Myanmar and Bangladesh**.
 
• Known for its unique Mizo culture, the state celebrates vibrant festivals such as **Chapchar Kut** and **Thalfavang Kut**.
 
• The lush green hills and pleasant climate make Mizoram a popular destination for eco-tourism.
 
 
 
• **Foundation Day Celebrations:**
 
 
• The foundation day of Arunachal Pradesh and Mizoram is marked by cultural events, parades, and official ceremonies to commemorate their journey as independent states.
 
• It is an occasion to reflect on their development, achievements, and the preservation of their unique heritage.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Historical Developments:**

 
 
• The **State Reorganization Act** of **1987** was crucial in granting statehood to Arunachal Pradesh and Mizoram.
 
• Both states were granted full statehood to address regional demands, ensure better governance, and promote socio-economic development.
 
 
 
• **Role of Article 3:**
 
 
• Article 3 of the Indian Constitution empowers the Parliament to create new states or alter existing ones based on socio-political needs.
 
• The process involves consultation with the state legislature and approval by the President.

questions.question: How is a long and healthy life measured in HDI?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Life expectancy at birth**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Life expectancy at birth** is a fundamental indicator used to measure the "long and healthy life" component of the **Human Development Index (HDI)**.
 
• It estimates the average number of years a newborn is expected to live, assuming that current mortality rates remain constant throughout their life.
 
• This metric reflects the overall health conditions of a population, including factors such as access to healthcare, nutrition, and living standards.
 
• A higher life expectancy signifies better health outcomes, indicating a higher level of human development.
 
• **HDI** uses life expectancy at birth as it provides a comprehensive overview of mortality rates across different age groups and regions. *Hence, this is the correct option.*
 
• Other aspects like **number of doctors, access to hospitals, and health insurance coverage** are important, but they are not direct measures used in HDI calculations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **About Human Development Index (HDI):**

 
 
• HDI is a composite measure introduced by the **United Nations Development Programme (UNDP)** in its **Human Development Report (HDR) of 1990**.
 
• It evaluates three critical dimensions of human development: **health (measured by life expectancy at birth), education (measured by mean years of schooling and expected years of schooling), and standard of living (measured by Gross National Income per capita).**
 
 
 
• **Life Expectancy at Birth:**
 
 
• This is the average number of years a newborn is expected to live, assuming current mortality rates continue to apply.
 
• It is influenced by factors such as access to healthcare, quality of medical facilities, nutrition, and socio-economic conditions.
 
 
 
• **Features of Other Options:**
 
 
• **Number of Doctors:** While an important indicator of healthcare infrastructure, it does not directly measure life expectancy or health outcomes.
 
• **Access to Hospitals:** This reflects healthcare availability but does not provide a direct measure of a population's overall health or longevity.
 
• **Health Insurance Coverage:** This indicates the financial accessibility of healthcare but does not directly impact the long and healthy life measure in HDI.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Global Trends:**

 
 
• According to the **2020 Human Development Report**, the global average life expectancy was approximately **73.4 years**.
 
• Countries with higher HDI rankings, such as **Norway, Switzerland, and Ireland**, exhibit higher life expectancy due to their advanced healthcare systems and socio-economic conditions.
 
 
 
• **India’s Position:**
 
 
• India’s life expectancy at birth was around **70 years (2021 data)**, reflecting significant improvement over the past decades due to better healthcare access and policies.
 
• India ranks in the **medium human development category** in the HDI index, with continuous efforts to improve healthcare and living standards.
 
 
 
• **Significance:**
 
 
• Life expectancy at birth is an essential indicator as it directly correlates with health and socio-economic policies in a country.
 
• It helps policymakers assess the effectiveness of healthcare systems and identify areas requiring improvement.

questions.question: As per the Press Information Bureau release dated March 10, 2025, what is a major feature of the Bills of Lading Bill, 2025?

options.text: Fixing freight rates for maritime shipments
Replacing paper bills with biometric authentication
Modernising India's maritime laws by replacing the old law
Mandating insurance for all cargo vessels

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Modernising India's maritime laws by replacing the old law**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Bills of Lading Bill, 2025** was introduced as a major step to modernize **India's maritime laws** by replacing the outdated legislation. This aligns with global practices and ensures that India adheres to international standards in shipping and logistics.
 
• The existing law governing **Bills of Lading** in India is considered outdated and does not address modern challenges in the shipping industry. By introducing this bill, India aims to streamline and update its legislative framework.
 
• The bill focuses on addressing key issues in the maritime sector, including **digitization**, **transparency**, and **efficiency**, which are essential for facilitating global trade and improving the country's logistics ecosystem.
 
• **Modernization of maritime laws** is critical for India, given its strategic location and the importance of maritime trade for the economy. This bill is expected to provide a robust framework for shipping operations, reduce disputes, and improve legal clarity.
 
• The bill also ensures better compliance with international conventions like the **United Nations Convention on Contracts for the International Carriage of Goods Wholly or Partly by Sea (Rotterdam Rules)**, which India is a signatory to.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is "Modernising India's maritime laws by replacing the old law."***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Bills of Lading:**

 
 
• A **Bill of Lading** is a legal document issued by a carrier to a shipper that serves as a contract of carriage, receipt of goods, and document of title.
 
• It is a crucial document in international trade, ensuring that goods are transported securely and that the rights of buyers, sellers, and carriers are protected.
 
• The modernization of laws governing Bills of Lading is essential to address issues like **fraud prevention**, **efficient dispute resolution**, and **digital documentation**.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Modernizing Maritime Laws:**
 
 
• India's current maritime laws are based on outdated colonial-era legislation, which no longer caters to the complexities of modern global trade.
 
• Modern laws will facilitate smoother operations for shipping companies and traders, reduce legal ambiguities, and ensure faster resolution of disputes.
 
• It will also enhance India's competitiveness in the global shipping industry and attract foreign investment in the logistics sector.
 
 
 
• **Key Features of the Bills of Lading Bill, 2025:**
 
 
• Incorporates provisions for **electronic Bills of Lading** to replace paper-based documents, promoting digitization in the maritime sector.
 
• Ensures compliance with international conventions like the **Rotterdam Rules**, which enhance uniformity in maritime laws across countries.
 
• Addresses issues like **liability of carriers**, **rights of shippers**, and **contractual obligations**, ensuring clarity and fairness in shipping operations.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Why Modernization is Needed:**

 
 
• The Indian shipping industry is growing rapidly, and outdated laws are a bottleneck to its efficiency and global competitiveness.
 
• The shift towards digitization is critical, as global shipping is moving towards paperless documentation to reduce costs and enhance security.
 
 
 
• **Other Key Developments in Indian Maritime Sector:**
 
 
• The **Sagarmala Project**, launched by the Indian government, aims to modernize ports and develop coastal infrastructure to support maritime trade.
 
• India has also been focusing on increasing its share in global shipping by improving port facilities and introducing investor-friendly policies.
